name: St. Mary Cathedral Basilica
architect: Theodore E. Giraud; later work by Nicholas J. Clayton
history: Bishop Jean-Marie Odin built a church here when Texas was a mission field. For the present church he bought 500,000 bricks from Belgium, shipped to Galveston as ballast. It was dedicated in 1848 and became the cathedral of the new Diocese of Galveston, the mother church of Catholics in Texas. It was named a minor basilica in 1979.
arch: Belgian brick in Gothic Revival style. A transept tower was added in 1876 and topped in 1878 with a cast-iron statue of Mary, Star of the Sea; the front spires were raised to 80 feet in 1886.
features: It survived the 1900 Galveston hurricane with little damage.
The cast-iron Star of the Sea statue has watched over the harbor since 1878.

look.d: The two front spires were raised to 80 feet in 1886.
These walls are made of bricks that crossed the Atlantic as ship's ballast.

fun: Many Galvestonians say the Star of the Sea statue protected the church in the 1900 storm. That's tradition, not a recorded fact.
